rich_text.plain_text: Scandinavian wall art earns its place in a living room by doing two things at once: bringing in warmth and character, and leaving the calm alone. Whether you live in a compact city flat or a spacious countryside home, Nordic artwork has a knack for anchoring a room without overwhelming it. The trick is understanding the principles behind Scandinavian design: simplicity, function and a deep connection to nature.

rich_text.plain_text: Start with your walls, not your art

text.content: Start with your walls, not your art

rich_text.plain_text: Before you start browsing prints, step back and look at your living room with fresh eyes. Consider the wall space you've actually got, the natural light that moves through the room during the day, and the existing palette of your furniture. Scandinavian interiors tend to favour neutral backgrounds, whites, soft greys and natural wood tones, which is a canvas waiting for artwork to stand out against.

rich_text.plain_text: The classic position. For a single statement piece, choose something roughly two-thirds the width of your sofa, and hang it so the centre of the artwork sits at eye level, around 145 to 150 cm from the floor, leaving 15 to 25 cm between the frame and the sofa back. If you prefer a gallery arrangement, keep the spacing between frames consistent at around 5 to 8 cm.

rich_text.plain_text: Framing: the finishing touch

text.content: Framing: the finishing touch

rich_text.plain_text: The frame isn't an afterthought; it's part of the artwork's presence in your room. In Scandinavian homes, a natural wood frame is the default choice, warm against the pale timber Nordic furniture leans on. Black frames create a clean, graphic look that suits contemporary spaces. White frames disappear into white walls, letting the artwork itself take centre stage. All three are chosen on each product page.

rich_text.plain_text: Mixing art styles the Scandinavian way

text.content: Mixing art styles the Scandinavian way

rich_text.plain_text: One of the hallmarks of Scandinavian interiors is the confident mixing of art styles. An abstract print beside a botanical beside a deadpan character illustration: it shouldn't work, but it does, because the unifying thread is the restraint and quality of each piece.

text.content: One of the hallmarks of Scandinavian interiors is the confident mixing of art styles. An abstract print beside a botanical beside a deadpan character illustration: it shouldn't work, but it does, because the unifying thread is the restraint and quality of each piece.

rich_text.plain_text: The trick is to vary the subject matter but keep the tone consistent. Choose pieces that all feel considered and intentional, and avoid anything that feels mass-produced or generic. Scandinavian design is fundamentally about authenticity, and that applies to the art on your walls as much as the furniture beneath it.
